Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:81: The third Gate, concerning the fitting food for union:
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:82: Know that according to each person's food shall the nourished body be - and by way of investigation it is known that the animal from which musk is drawn eats spikenard. Now, the Name, blessed be He, in all His ways is justice - He commanded to slaughter animals for food, and why should this be, when it would be better for us to be nourished by fruits and delicacies, and why should He allow the blood of animals and beasts to be shed and cause them great pain?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:83: Know that these are the foundations of the world: that the Name, blessed be He, does good to every creature, and has mercy on His creatures - and of this it is said (Psalms 145:9), "the LORD is good to all." One who knows this verse shall know that the slaughtering of living beings and their consumption by human beings is for the benefit of the living beings themselves, and is compassion and mercy toward them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:84: And I shall explain: it is known that all the food a person eats goes into the stomach, and from there descends to the upper intestines, and from there the liver draws out the good, the choicest, the richest, the purest, and the cleanest of that food, and pushes the rest to the lower intestines, and it exits through excretion - and that thing which the liver draws out returns and cooks it again, and it returns to every single organ, according to the kind of organ, in a third cooking, and it returns as flesh to flesh, fat to fat, sinew to sinew, and bone to bone, for from it the body is nourished. If so, that animal that was slaughtered was slaughtered for its own benefit, for it ascended from the level of an animal's body to the level of a human body.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:85: And this is the way of the four compositions of the lower world, which are: springs, plants, and speaking and non-speaking living beings. For springs draw and are nourished from the four elements, and plants are nourished from the four elements and from the springs. And non-speaking living beings are nourished from the plants and the springs and the four elements, and the speaking living being makes use of the non-speaking living beings and of the plants and of the springs and of the four elements - and so everything proceeds from elevation to elevation, until the cycle returns front and back. And of this it is said, "the LORD is good to all" - from the elements it ascends to a level above them, which are the springs; and the springs ascend to a level above them, which are the growing plants; and from the plants they ascend above them, which are the non-speaking living beings that move and grow and are composed of the four elements; and from the non-speaking living beings they ascend to a level greater than them, which are the speaking living beings, who possess the power of speech and the power of movement and the power of growth and the power of composition from the four elements. If so, it is found that all things become food for others in order to elevate them to a great elevation above their [own prior] level.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:86: And after this preface, know that since blood is the food of the body and refines the body, and blood is according to the nature of the food from which it is made - thick and turbid or fine - if the food is clean, pure, and refined, the blood shall be like it; and therefore He, blessed be He, set us apart, in His holy Torah, from several forbidden foods that He forbade to us: some of them numb the heart, like milk and blood [mixed forbidden combinations]; some of them harden the face, like beasts and birds and predatory animals; some of them close the doors of understanding and wisdom, like the hare, the hyrax, the pig, and their like; and some of them beget several kinds of harsh and evil illnesses, like the creeping things of the land and the water. In sum, concerning all of them He said (Leviticus 11:43), "do not make your souls detestable." Behold, He made known that all these things are repugnant and loathsome and make bad blood, prone to several punishments.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:87: Now, since it said that a person must sanctify himself at the time of relations, this holiness includes food as well, for it is fitting for a person to eat fit and proper foods, moderate between cold and heat, and that they be from things that beget clean, pure, and refined blood - since that blood is destined to be turned into the fineness of the seed, and it is destined to be the foundation and building-block for the offspring born from that union - for if the food were bad, turbid, and thick, the drop too would be thick, filthy, and turbid; and if so, it follows that the food for a person's coming into being is a preparation for him to be wise or foolish, righteous or wicked.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:88: And I hand to you a great key: know that, the matter being as we say, the Name, blessed be He, in His holy Torah juxtaposed the section "when a woman conceives" to the forbidden foods - saying (Leviticus 11:47), "to distinguish between the impure and the pure," and so on, and juxtaposed to it, "when a woman conceives" - and He juxtaposed, from another side, the section of afflictions [nega'im] - and these three sections have wondrous secrets, with the section "when she conceives" in the middle, to make known that if a person separates himself from bad foods he shall have proper, holy, and pure children, and if not, then afflictions are renewed upon them because of the drop of seed that came from those repugnant foods - and therefore it comes to make known to you that a person must sanctify himself also with proper foods close to relations, so that the seed be clean and pure and moderate, between north and south, as we have said.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:89: Now, we have made known to you that according to the food shall be the blood produced, and according to the blood shall be the seed, and according to the seed shall be the offspring born from it - and you already know what we have said, that an eagle is not born from a horse, nor lentils from wheat - so too we say that from turbid and bad seed nothing is born but detestable, repugnant blood, as it says (Psalms 58:4), "the wicked are estranged from the womb."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:90: Now, we have made known to you, in this way, the way of proper food - and it is fitting for us to tell you that of proper food one need not take an amount to fill the body, but only a moderate amount that nature can grind, and that shall quickly turn into clean and pure blood - for when food increases in the stomach, even if it be from proper things, its increase shall cause it not to be ground and to spoil in the stomach, and it shall turn out worse and filthier than if it had been from coarse and bad things. Therefore one must be careful also with the measure of food, just as one is careful with the substance of the food itself. Behold, guard this great principle, which is arranged from the side of food toward the side of union.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:91: The fourth Gate, concerning the intent of union:
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:92: What they, of blessed memory, said (Yoma 29a) - a great secret - "thoughts of transgression are harder [worse] than transgression itself" - and I shall enlighten your eyes with matters that are the depths of the world, hidden in several inner chambers. Know that the Name, blessed be He, God of knowledge, established His actions with perfect wisdom, and gave every single nature among the natures of the world a specific action of the thing entrusted to it as a fixed charge, without change, except by way of a miracle - and He gave power to man's imagination to beget the likeness of the thing he imagines, and we know this also from the aspect of nature. Now, when a person unites with his wife, if his imagination and his thoughts are occupied with wisdom, understanding, and good and proper attributes, then that imagination in his thoughts has the power to form the shape in the drop of seed just as he was imagining at the time of union, without doubt - and this is the secret of (Genesis 30:37), "and Jacob took himself rods of fresh poplar," and so on, and it says, "and the flocks were in heat before the rods," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:93: And our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said in Berachot (see page 20a, and see Bava Metzia 84a): Rabbi Yochanan used to go and sit at the gates of the ritual bath, saying, when the daughters of Israel come up from the river, they gaze at me so that they shall have offspring as handsome as I am. Contemplate this teaching: this pious man made known that when the woman thinks of his beauty as she comes up from the immersion, and unites with her husband, she shall form the shape of the child according to the imagination she pictures - and if so, imagination is found to be a great cause, and thought and imagination cause the offspring and his character, as we have explained. Behold, that thought and imagination cause the child to be righteous or wicked, just as food causes it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:94: And every person must clean his thoughts and imaginings and refine them at the time of relations, and should not be thinking of a matter of transgression and licentiousness, but rather of holy matters, and should think of the pure righteous, men of knowledge, intellect, and wisdom - for those thoughts shall rest upon the seed and form it in their image at the time of relations. And likewise his wife's thought: she should be gladdened with things that gladden the heart, so that she too be in agreement with clean and pure thoughts, and both of them shall be united in the matter of the mitzvah - for then their thought shall be bound as one, and the Shechinah shall rest between them, and they shall beget a son according to the pure form they pictured.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:95: And do not wonder at this matter, for it is a simple nature in the eyes of the sages of investigation - that according to the thought and imagining that pass over the heart of a man and his wife at the time of their union, the offspring shall be prepared and found, whether good or bad. And they already brought (see Bereishit Rabbah 73:10) the story of that noblewoman who bore a black son, though she and the king were both very fair, and the king thought to kill her, until a certain sage came and said to him, perhaps she thought, at the time of relations, of a black man - and they examined and found black figures in the decorations of that room in which she had relations, and she said that she had been gazing at those figures and thinking of them at the time of union - and this is like the matter of the rods.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:96: And do not wonder, for something greater than this is known from nature: a person bitten by a rabid dog, who becomes ill with the illness known from that bite - from the very imagination he pictures in his mind, they cannot bring water before him, for he shall immediately imagine that there are rabid dogs in it, and even in his urine one shall see the very shape of vicious dogs, because of the abundance of imagining and confusion, marking his imaginings and his confusion in the urine. Understand this very well, and see how far the power of picturing and imagining reaches at the time of relations.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:97: In sum, when a person imagines good and pure things, that good imagining rests upon the drop of seed, and the offspring shall be formed in the shape of that imagining, and shall be destined to be a wholly righteous person - of him it is said (Jeremiah 1:5), "before I formed you in the belly," and so on; and in truth, before his form comes to be, the good imagining is ready to form him, and then the Shechinah participates with the pure thought, as they, of blessed memory, said (Kiddushin 40a), a good thought - the Holy One, blessed be He, joins it to the deed. And if a person thinks of a matter of transgression and ugliness, the offspring is founded upon a foundation of wickedness and ugliness, and shall be destined to be a filthy wicked person - of him it is said (Psalms 58:4), "the wicked are estranged from the womb."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:98: And I must arouse you concerning a great foundation, found in the Torah and in the words of our Rabbis, of blessed memory: "God settles the solitary in a home" (Psalms 68:7) - and they, of blessed memory, said, whoever marries a woman for the sake of beauty - a new [child] enters and a new one leaves and a sword consumes him, as it is said (Hosea 5:7), "they have betrayed the LORD, for they have begotten strange children." The great secret in this is that when he marries a woman for the sake of beauty, his union is not for the sake of Heaven, for indeed he is imagining her form in a bodily way, and does not think with a pure, supernal thought - and so the son born from that imagining is a foreign and strange son, and of him it is said, "for they have begotten strange children," and the Name has no portion in him - they are found to be traitors, and the Shechinah departs from between them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:99: And I have come to arouse in you a great principle: know that this is why the section of the stubborn and rebellious son and the section of the hanged one are juxtaposed to the section of the beautiful captive woman - for from a woman taken captive, a righteous person shall not emerge, since the intent was only for beauty and licentiousness; there shall emerge from her rebellious and stubborn sons, fit for the four death penalties of the court. And know that it was not for nothing that the matter of Tamar and Absalom happened to David, for both of them were children of "beautiful captive women," for all this is caused by imagining the very form pictured [at the time of conception]. If so, understand from what we have aroused you to in this chapter, concerning the matter of the intent of union and thought and imagining.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:100: And I wish to arouse you concerning a great principle, and to hand you a great gift, in the secret of thought - how it acts upon the form of the matter from which it is received. Behold, our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Yoma 29a), thoughts of transgression are harder than transgression itself, and elsewhere they said (Kiddushin 40a), an evil thought - the Holy One, blessed be He, does not join it to a deed, except for idolatry, as it is said (Ezekiel 14:5), "in order to take hold of the house of Israel by their heart."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:101: And I shall enlighten your eyes with matters that come sealed in the Gemara. Behold, they, of blessed memory, said (Vayikra Rabbah 16:4; Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:10), Ben Azzai was sitting and studying, and fire was blazing around him; and Rabbi Eliezer was sitting and expounding, and rays shone from him like the rays of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him (Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer, chapter 2). And you shall need to know that all these matters have one intent, and I shall explain: a spring of water, when drawn from a high place to a low place, has the power to raise those waters to another high place, corresponding to the height of the water's source. And so it is known, God willing, that a person's thought is from the source of the intellectual soul drawn from the supernal beings, and thought has the power to spread and ascend and reach up to the place of its emergence - and upon reaching the source, it then cleaves to the supernal secret from which it is drawn, and it and it become one thing; and when the thought returns to be drawn from above to below, everything becomes like the likeness of one line, and that supernal light is drawn downward, and then the bright light is drawn and spreads in that place where the possessor of the thought is sitting. And so the early pious ones would cleave their thought to the supernal beings and draw the supernal light down, and through this things would increase and multiply according to the power of the thought - and this is the secret of the oil of Elisha, peace be upon him, and the jar of flour and the jug of oil of Elijah.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:102: And since the matter is so, our Rabbis, of blessed memory, needed to say that when a person unites with his wife and his thought cleaves to the supernal beings, that very thought draws supernal light downward, and it rests upon that drop that he intends and imagines - along the lines of the jug - and that drop is found bound forever to the bright light; and this is the secret of "before" (Jeremiah 1:5), "I formed you in the belly," and so on - because the bright light had already been bound to that righteous man's drop at the time of union, since the thought was bound to the supernal beings and drew the bright light. Understand this very well, and you shall understand from it a great secret in the matter of "God of Abraham, God of Isaac, and God of Jacob" - and there it is said that at the time they were occupied with eating and drinking and marital relations and other bodily matters, what should become of it [their attachment to Him]? And the answer was that even in all bodily matters, their whole intent was for the sake of Heaven, and their thought never separated from the supernal light even for a single moment - and through this Jacob merited to beget twelve tribes, all of them wholly righteous and perfect, fit to be the likeness of the orders of the world, bearers of the vessels of the LORD, since their thought never separated from the supernal light even at the time of union.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:103: And therefore Solomon, peace be upon him, said (Proverbs 3:6), "know Him in all your ways" - and this knowing is the joining of the intellectual soul, cleaving to the supernal light, and it is not called "knowing" a certain thing until the intellect cleaves to the object of intellect.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:104: And after we have made this known to you, contemplate why thoughts of transgression are harder than transgression itself - for when a person thinks of wicked and filthy matters, his thought cleaves in its filth to the supernal beings, and behold his soul is thereby liable to Heaven, for it becomes impure through contact - but had he performed the transgression below, and its judgment had not touched Heaven, it would be lighter upon him than an evil thought, which is close to "cutting the shoots" [heresy]. And from this you shall understand the secret of "thoughts of transgression are harder than transgression itself": one who thinks a forbidden thought at the time of relations - that filthy thought rests upon the drop, and founds from it a foundation of wickedness, iniquity, and filth, and it is called "strange." And from this you shall understand the deed of that pious man who sat at the gates of the ritual bath, so that their thought and imagining be bound to his form, and his form be bound to the supernal beings.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:105: Further, we shall make known to you another matter concerning thought, which although it is not for the intent of union, nevertheless is beneficial to him and to others - namely, that when the holy pious ones would bind their thought to the supernal beings, whatever matter they thought about at that hour would be established, whether for good or for evil - and this is what it said (Berachot 58a), "he set his eyes on him and he became a heap of bones"; and it is written in Ta'anit (24a), in that baraita, "return to your dust," and so it happened; and what it said (Chagigah 5b), any place upon which the Sages set their eyes, either death or poverty [results]. And from this matter is the secret of prayer and of sacrifices, which is the secret of cleaving to the supernal beings.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:106: And from this matter came the power of that accursed wicked Balaam, of whom they would say (Numbers 22:6), "he whom you bless is blessed," and so on - and therefore he wished to gaze at Israel with a complete gaze, in order to be able to bind his thought to the supernal beings and draw down upon them an evil thought, and therefore it says (Numbers 24:2), "and Balaam lifted his eyes," and so on - and therefore he needed to be precise, "come now with me to another place, from which you shall see them," and so on (ibid. 23:13) - for the wicked one needed to gaze at that toward which his intent was directed, for good or for evil, and he would bind his thought above and draw supernal power to whomever he intended and gazed at - and this is the matter of (ibid. 24:4), "who beholds the vision of Shaddai, falling, but with eyes uncovered." And therefore the wicked one intended to build seven altars, with a bull and a ram on each one, in order to draw into himself all the powers and bring them near to his thought, in order to fulfill his evil desire and will in whatever he craved. And for this it says (Numbers 23:14), "and he took him to the field of Zophim [watchers]" - for the wicked one would watch them in order to draw down upon them his evil thought. But the Holy One, blessed be He, who knows all thoughts, knew his evil thought, and did not allow it for the will of the wicked Balaam. Understand this very well, and know how far the power of thought reaches.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:107: And after we have made known to you these sealed secrets, we have yet to make known to you the secret of the next way, as fitting, with the help of the LORD.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:108: The fifth Gate, concerning the manner of union:
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:109: It is known that every pious and modest man, when he speaks, speaks only in a gentle tongue and soft speech and with calmness of spirit, and does not speak boastfully, and when he walks, he walks with a bent stature and a lowered head, and so in all his conduct; while the wicked one, in all his ways, is the opposite of this. And you must consider: since matters that have no disgrace in an organ among people [are still treated with modesty], all the more so a matter of disgrace in an organ and disgrace in a deed - and therefore, whenever a person unites with a woman, he should not be lightheaded or use vain and deceitful words, and should not be lighthearted toward the woman, nor engage much in idle talk with her.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:110: And therefore you should first engage her with words that draw her heart and settle her mind and gladden her, so that her mind be bound with your mind and her intent with your intent - tell her words, some of which draw her toward desire, love, and willingness, and some of which draw her toward fear of Heaven, piety, and modesty - and speak with her about pious and modest women, how they produced from themselves proper and fit children, worthy masters of Torah, fear of Heaven, and rendering of instruction - such as the story of Kimchit, who merited seven sons, all of whom served as High Priest, and our Sages, of blessed memory, asked her by what she merited this, and she said to them, even the beams of my house never saw the hair of my head in my days (Yoma 47a) - and all this she attained as reward for her modesty and piety and the uprightness of her deeds. And he should speak with her in the middle of the night, or close to the last third, as it is taught in Berachot (3a), in the third watch, a baby nurses from its mother's breast and a wife speaks with her husband.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:111: In sum, when you examine yourself and see that you are fit to have relations, examine also your wife's mind and bring her to agree with your mind, and when you unite, do not rush to arouse desire in her, so that her mind may settle. And from all the matters we have made known to you in the previous words, and along this way, you should infer several matters that we have not mentioned from among the matters we have mentioned, and include all of them. And from your own understanding you shall grasp the manner of conduct proper for a person at the time of relations, more modestly than all the modesty you observe in all your habits regarding food, drink, and worldly conduct - for according to the modesty and thought you conduct at the time of union, so shall the form rest upon the drop of seed.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:112: And this is the secret of (Genesis 25:19), "and these are the generations of Isaac, son of Abraham," and so on - meaning, after the Holy One, blessed be He, told him that Sarah his wife would bear him a son, Abraham intended, at the time of union, an intent surpassing all his other good qualities, binding his thought to the supernal beings and intending to beget a son who would be fit for what the Holy One, blessed be He, had told him - and this is the secret of "Abraham begot Isaac": he intended to beget a son who would be wholly righteous like himself. And this is the secret of "Abraham begot" - they, of blessed memory, said (Bereishit Rabbah 63:1), a righteous man, son of a righteous man - and the power of his righteousness reached so far that the Holy One, blessed be He, testified that there was no blemish in him, neither within nor without - and this is the secret of (Genesis 22:2), "and offer him up there as a burnt offering" - and you already know that it was not fitting for there to be a blemish in a thing offered upon the altar. Understand this great teaching. And you already know that the burnt offering is the Holy of Holies (Zevachim, chapter 5, mishnah 5), and it comes for a sinful thought of the heart (Vayikra Rabbah 7:3) and for sins perceptible [only in intent] (Yoma 36a), and therefore it needs flaying and cutting up - and Isaac is called "a perfect burnt offering" (Bereishit Rabbah 64:3) - and all this was caused by Abraham at the time of union, that he intended truly for the sake of Heaven.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:113: And so the matter applies to the rest of the pious, men of heart: when they intend for the sake of a mitzvah, to bind their thought to the supernal beings at the time of union, then they beget children fit for holiness, purity, and piety. And therefore the Scroll of Ruth needed to write (Ruth 4:18), "these are the generations of Peretz: Peretz begot Chetzron" - since Peretz, a wholly righteous man, also intended to beget a righteous son like himself, and this is the secret of "Peretz begot Chetzron" - and so on until "Jesse begot David," a righteous man, son of a righteous man, to make known that it was not for nothing that the Holy One, blessed be He, chose David His servant - for it is a chain of ten wholly righteous men, one above the other, in the likeness of the ten orders of the world, in the secret of the Yud, since from Peretz to David there are ten generations, righteous man, son of righteous man. And now, contemplate the secret of what we have summarized in these matters, and when you conduct yourself by them as we have made known to you, I guarantee you that you shall beget a righteous, pious son who sanctifies the Name of Heaven. To this point are the words of the Ramban, of blessed memory.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 16:114: And anyone who does not marry a fit woman and does not beget children is considered as dead (see Nedarim 64b), and anyone who begets fit children, even though he has died, is as though alive - as we learn in Bava Batra (116a): Rabbi Yitzchak bar Chama expounded, what is the meaning of what is written (I Kings 11:21), "that David slept with his fathers" and "that Joab, the general, was dead"? Why is "sleeping" said of David and "death" of Joab? David, who left a son, "sleeping" is said of him; Joab, who did not leave a son, "death" is said of him. But did Joab not leave a son? Is it not written, "and of the sons of Joab, Ovadiah son of Yechiel"? Rather, David, who left a son like himself, "sleeping" is said of him; Joab, who did not leave a son like himself, "death" is said of him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:1: After having spoken of the holiness of the covenant, we must explain what blemishes it, and what its remedy shall be. First we shall speak of the matter of emitting seed in vain, which is the most common, for hardly any person in our generation escapes it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:2: And in Tractate Niddah (13a) they were strict about the severity of this sin - these are their words themselves: Rabbi Eliezer says, whoever holds his membrum and urinates is as though he brings a flood upon the world. They said to Rabbi Eliezer, but sparks fly onto his feet, and it appears as though his member is severed [i.e., he must hold it to avoid this appearance], and it follows that he casts a slur upon his children, that they are mamzerim [illegitimate]? He said to them, better that he cast a slur upon his children, that they are mamzerim, than that he make himself wicked for one moment before the Omnipresent. It is taught in another baraita: Rabbi Eliezer said to the Sages, could a person stand in a high place and urinate, or urinate into loose earth, and not make himself wicked for one moment before the Omnipresent? Which did he say first? If you say the first [about holding the member], he said them in this order: after he told them the prohibition, he told them the remedy; rather, he must have said this [about the high place and loose earth] first. But they said to him, what if he has no high place or loose earth? He said to them, better that he cast a slur upon his children than that he make himself wicked for one moment before the Omnipresent.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:3: And why all this? Because he thereby emits seed in vain - for Rabbi Yochanan said, whoever emits seed in vain is liable for death, as it is said (Genesis 38:10), "and what he did was evil in the eyes of the LORD, and He put him to death also." Rabbi Yitzchak and Rabbi Ami say, it is as though he sheds blood, as it is said (Isaiah 57:5), "who inflame yourselves among the terebinths, under every green tree, who slaughter [shochtei] the children in the valleys, under the clefts of the rocks" - do not read "shochtei" [who slaughter] but "sochtei" [who squeeze out]. Rav Ashi said, it is as though he worships idols - it is written here, "under every green tree," and it is written there (Deuteronomy 12:2), "upon the high mountains and under every green tree."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:4: Further, it said shortly after (13b): Rav said, whoever hardens himself deliberately shall be placed under a ban. But let it say [simply], it is forbidden? Because he thereby incites the evil inclination against himself. And Rabbi Ami said, he is called an apostate, for such is the craft of the evil inclination: today it tells him, do such and such, and tomorrow it tells him, do such and such, and the next day it tells him, go worship idols, and he goes and worships. Some say Rabbi Ami said, whoever brings himself to a state of forbidden thought is not admitted into the enclosure of the Holy One, blessed be He - it is written here (Genesis 38:10), "and what he did was evil in the eyes of the LORD," and it is written there (Psalms 5:5), "for You are not a God who desires wickedness; evil shall not sojourn with You." And Rabbi Elazar said, what is the meaning of (Isaiah 1:15), "your hands are full of blood"? These are those who commit adultery with the hand. It was taught in the school of Rabbi Yishmael, "you shall not commit adultery" - there shall be no adultery in you, whether by hand or by foot. Our Rabbis taught: proselytes and those who play with children delay the Messiah - and they explained there in the Gemara that this refers to those who marry young girls not yet able to bear children, for Rabbi Yosei said, the son of David does not come until all the souls in the [heavenly] body [treasury] are exhausted, as it is said (Isaiah 57:16), "for the spirit would grow faint before Me, and the souls I have made" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:5: And in Tractate Kallah (chapter 1) they said: Rabbi says, "who inflame yourselves among the terebinths" (Isaiah 57:5) - whoever heats himself to emit seed in vain is considered like an animal: just as an animal is concerned only about being slaughtered and has no portion in the World to Come, so he has no portion in the World to Come - and of him Solomon said in his wisdom (Ecclesiastes 3:21), "who knows the spirit of the children of man, whether it goes upward" - this is the soul of the righteous, who do not heat themselves and do not emit seed in vain; "and the spirit of the animal, whether it goes down to the earth" - this is the soul of the wicked, who heat themselves and emit seed in vain. Whoever heats himself is liable for death, and whoever hardens himself [deliberately] is an apostate, as it is said (Genesis 38:10), "and what he did was evil in the eyes of the LORD" - to this point.
